get.description:
Returns a report comparing the budget and forecast to the actual spend.

The response is similar to the rows returned by the `costs/aggregated` API.

Each row represents a specific combination of dimension values and timestamp, and includes the corresponding budget amount, forecast amount, actual spend amount and variance (between forecast and actual).

The API also expects the user to have cost access to the segments in the report. If the budget uses billing center level dimensions, access to each row/segment
is determined by the user's access to costs on the billing center. If the budget doesn't use billing center level dimensions, then the user is expected to have
cost access at the org level.

By default, the report contains one row for each combination of budget segment and year-month. 
For example, for a budget with 10 budget segments covering 12 months, 
the report would return 120 rows (i.e., 10 segments * 12 months).

### Budgeted and Unbudgeted spend
All rows include a `budgeted` dimension with a boolean value.
It is `false` only if the row contains new dimension values from the cost data that were not described by the budget segments.

For example, if a budget defines segments for 2 specific account values, for those rows the `budgeted` dimension will be `true`.

If a 3rd account appears in the billing data, its row will be returned with the `budgeted` dimension set to `false`.

This allows you to identify the unbudgeted spend from the 3rd account. You may then wish to either:
- update the budget segments to cover the new account,
- or modify the budget's filter expression to exclude the account.

### Filtering
To narrow the report to a specific range of year-months, specify the start and end dates in the filter query parameter.

By default, the budget report returns all the budgeted and unbudgeted rows.
- Set the `budgeted` parameter to `true` to return only budgeted rows.
- Set the `budgeted` parameter to `false` to return only unbudgeted rows.

### Aggregation across budget segments
The report API can sum up results based on the requested `dimensions`.

For example, consider a budget broken down by two dimensions: Vendor and Account.

- If the `dimensions` list includes both Vendor and Account, the report will display the full budget details, with rows for potentially dozens of accounts.
- If the `dimensions` list includes only Vendor, the report will return fewer rows, providing a summary of the budget, forecast, actual spend and variance for each vendor.
- If the `dimensions` list is empty, the report will return just one row for each year-month, summarizing the total budget, forecast, actual spend and variance across all budget segments.

### Aggregation across year-months

The report API can also sum up results across year-months.

By default, it returns one row for each budget segment and year-month combination.

However, by setting the `summarized` parameter to `true`,
the report will return only one row per budget segment, 
representing its total budget, forecast, spend and variance across all the selected year-months.

tags.description:
See: [https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Optima/cloudbudgets.htm](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Optima/cloudbudgets.htm)

The Budget API provides functionality for both Budgeting and Forecasting, enabling users to analyze planned budgets and forecasts against actual spend.

The API allows you to create, read, update, and delete budgets, as well as generate budget reports to compare your planned budget and forecast with actual spend. Budgets are defined using a combination of dimensions, year-months, and segments to provide a flexible and detailed breakdown of your costs.

A budget is defined with the following properties:

- `name`: A descriptive name to uniquely identify the budget.
- `metric`: The cost metric used for the budget, such as `cost_amortized_unblended_adj`.
- `dimensions`: An array of dimensions used for budget breakdown, such as `vendor_account`, or `rbd_team`.
- `yearMonths`: An array of year-month strings like `"2023-01"`, defining the time period covered by the budget.
- `segments`: An array of budget segments, like rows in a spreadsheet. Each segment describes a combination of dimension values and the corresponding budget amount and forecast amount for each year-month.
- `filter`: An optional filter expression to narrow down the scope of the budget based on specific dimension values. This is useful later when generating a budget report, as it allows you to exclude certain line items from the report rather than marking them as "unbudgeted". For example, you might define the budget filter to only include AWS costs, and exclude all Tax line items from the budget.

Here's an example budget for "2023 Q1" listing the expected costs for each vendor, for the first three months of the year:
```json
{
  "name": "2023 Q1",
  "metric": "cost_amortized_unblended_adj",
  "dimensions": ["vendor"],
  "yearMonths": ["2023-01", "2023-02", "2023-03"],
  "segments": [
    {"dimensionValues": ["AWS"], "budgetAmounts": [100, 110, 120], "forecastAmounts":  [110, 100, 130]},
    {"dimensionValues": ["GCP"], "budgetAmounts": [200, 230, 240], "forecastAmounts":  [210, 200, 230]}
  ]
}
```

For full details on the budget properties, please refer to the Budget CRUD actions below.

## Decentralized Access
The Budget API allows decentralized access to budget reports by controlling access at the segment level. It does this by leveraging the existing billing center privileges.

The "Billing Center Level" dimensions (ex: "Billing Center Level 1") can be used in budgets to enable this behaviour, since they identify which billing center the costs are assigned to.

Let's consider an organization with the following billing center hierarchy: 
- Oaktree
  - Marketing
  - Engineering
  - Sales
    - Support
- Redwood
  - R & D
  - Marketing

The Billing Center Level dimensions would be populated with these combinations of values, representing the path that the costs were assigned to.

| Billing Center Level 1 | Billing Center Level 2 | Billing Center Level 3 |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| Oaktree                | Marketing              |                        |
| Oaktree                | Engineering            |                        |
| Oaktree                | Sales                  | Support                |
| Redwood                | R & D                  |                        |
| Redwood                | Marketing              |                        |

Note: the values would actually be billing center IDs, but here we'll use the billing center names for legibility.

A budget created with a Billing Center Level dimension will control access to reports at the segment level.

Here, we'll modify the above "2023 Q1" budget to be further broken down by the "Billing Center Level 1" dimension:
```json
{
  "name": "2023 Q1",
  "metric": "cost_amortized_unblended_adj",
  "dimensions": ["bc_level_1", "vendor"],
  "yearMonths": ["2023-01", "2023-02", "2023-03"],
  "segments": [
    {"dimensionValues": ["Oaktree", "AWS"], "budgetAmounts": [50,   55,  60]},
    {"dimensionValues": ["Oaktree", "GCP"], "budgetAmounts": [100, 115, 120]},
    {"dimensionValues": ["Redwood", "AWS"], "budgetAmounts": [55,   60,  65]},
    {"dimensionValues": ["Redwood", "GCP"], "budgetAmounts": [100, 115, 120]}
  ]
}
```

Since each segment is "assigned" to a billing center, different users will only see segments that they have access to:
- A user that doesn't have access to "Oaktree" or "Redwood" billing centers will not be able to see anything in the report.
- A user with access only to "Oaktree" will see just the first two segments in the report.
- A user with access only to "Redwood" will see only the last two segments in the report.
- A user with org-level access will see all of the segments, since they have access to both "Oaktree" and "Redwood".

## Budget JSON Editor UI

There is a prototype, standalone tool for editing budget JSON. It provides an interactive UI that enables you to visualize, edit, and validate budget JSON data:

- [Budget JSON Editor UI](https://s3-us-west-1.amazonaws.com/rs-api-docs/bill_analysis/budget_json_editor/index.html)

Features:

- **Two-way editing**: The editor displays the budget JSON on the left side and an editable UI representation on the right side. Changes made in either view are automatically reflected in the other.

- **Spreadsheet integration**: You can copy the budget table to a spreadsheet or paste content from a spreadsheet, making it easy to convert between formats.

- **Local validation**: The JSON data is validated locally in the browser, ensuring compatibility with the budget API.

## Budget Reports
The API also includes a powerful "Report" action, which allows you to generate a detailed report comparing your budget, forecast with actual spend. The report can be filtered by date range, aggregated across dimensions, and even include unbudgeted spend to identify new costs not covered by your existing budget.

For more information, please refer to the description for the `budgets/{id}/report` action, below.

tags.description:
This API gives Flexera One customers visibility into the cloud vendor accounts associated with their bills.

This data comes from scraping information from the cloud vendors once per day.
For each bill connect in the org, details are gathered for its associated accounts.
The account tags may be particularly useful, as bill data does not typically include account tag information.

Currently, only bills from Amazon Web Services (AWS) are supported.
